{{nihongo|'''Hakusan Shrine'''|白山神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Echigo Province]].

'''Hakusan Shrine''' (はくさんじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} at 1-1-17 Nuttari-higashi, {{ill|Chūō-ku, Niigata|Q711787|qid=Q711787|lt=Chūō Ward}}, {{ill|Niigata (city)|Q179691|qid=Q179691}}, {{ill|Niigata Prefecture|Q132705|qid=Q132705}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}. To distinguish it from the {{ill|Hakusan Shrine|Q11579595|qid=Q11579595|lt=shrine of the same name}} in Ichibanbori-dōri-chō, Chūō Ward, Niigata City, it is called “Nuttari Hakusan Shrine.”

=== Enshrined deities ===
As of 2019, the enshrined deities are as follows:
* '''{{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}}'''<ref name="現地情報">On-site information, dated April 13, 2019.</ref>
* '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kikurihime-no-Mikoto}}'''<ref name="ぬったり122p"/> - deity of harmony, bonds, and living water<ref name="現地情報"/>. Also called Hakusan-hime<ref name="沼垂記6p"/>.

=== History ===
The founding date is unknown<ref name="ぬったり122p"/>. According to shrine tradition, it was once called '''Mikuri Shrine'''<ref name="沼垂記6p">{{Cite book|ja|author=Niigata City Nuttari Library |title=Nuttari-ki |publisher=Niigata City Nuttari Library |year=1965 |page=6 |isbn=}}</ref>. It corresponds to '''Mikuri Shrine''' in Nuttari District, {{ill|Echigo Province|Q666514|qid=Q666514}}, recorded in the '''Engishiki Jinmyōchō'''<ref name="神社辞典">{{Cite book|ja|author=Shirai Eiji, Toki Masanori |title=Jinja Jiten (Shrine Dictionary) |publisher=Tōkyōdō Shuppan |year=1979 |page=273 |isbn=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|ja|author=Nuttari Local History Study Group |title=Nuttari Monogatari |publisher=Niigata City Nuttari Library |year=1965 |page=2 |isbn=}}</ref>, but no source materials from the time of its founding remain<ref name="合併町村の歴史168p"/>.

ზუღა|zh|日本海|zh_classical|鯨海|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún-hái|zh_yue|日本海|qid=Q27092}}. “Mikuri” means water distribution, and is a deity of {{ill|Irrigation|Q11453|qid=Q11453}}<ref name="沼垂記6p"/>. In the early Edo period (Kan'ei era), Nuttari Hakusan Shrine was in Ōse-yama<ref group="注">Present-day Yamanoshita.</ref><ref name="合併町村の歴史168p">{{Cite book|ja|author= |title=History of villages merged into Niigata City, Vol. 3 |publisher=Niigata City |year=1980 |page=168 |isbn=}}</ref> and served as the general tutelary shrine of the Nuttari area<ref name="ぬったり122p"/>. Due to repeated flooding of the Shinano River, it was forced to relocate many times<ref name="ぬったり122p"/><ref name="合併町村の歴史">{{Cite book|ja|author= |title=History of villages merged into Niigata City, Vol. 3 |publisher=Niigata City |year=1980 |page=170 |isbn=}}</ref>. In May {{ill|1706|Q6835|qid=Q6835}} ({{ill|Hōei|Q1145262|qid=Q1145262}} 3), it moved to the western side of Rui-chi. Later, in {{ill|1714|Q6878|qid=Q6878}} ({{ill|Shōtoku (era)|Q1193848|qid=Q1193848|lt=Shōtoku}} 4), it moved further east, and in {{ill|1725|Q6932|qid=Q6932}} ({{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} 10)<ref name="通史198p">{{Cite book|ja|author=Niigata City History Editorial Committee (Ancient/Medieval section) |title=Niigata City History, General History 1 |publisher=Niigata City |year=1995 |page=198 |isbn=}}</ref> or {{ill|1726|Q6936|qid=Q6936}} (Kyōhō 11)<ref name="ぬったり122p"/>, it settled at its current location<ref name="合併町村の歴史"/>. Shrine treasures such as deity statues, ritual implements, and old books were lost through repeated flood damage and relocations<ref name="ぬったり122p"/>.

It was formerly a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}<ref name="神社辞典"/> and is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}<ref name="現地情報"/>. There are two Shikinaisha in Nuttari: Nuttari Hakusan Shrine and Goshiki Shrine ({{ill|Kanbara Shrine (Q63148107)|Q63148107|qid=Q63148107|lt=Kambara Shrine}})<ref name="ぬったり122p"/>.

It is said that in the era of the {{ill|Uesugi clan|Q1150058|qid=Q1150058}}, 100 koku of shrine land were donated, but records from {{ill|1698|Q7706|qid=Q7706}} ({{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 11) state “shrine land: 10 koku”<ref>{{Cite book|ja|author= |title=Kyōdo Niigata No.1 |publisher=Niigata Local History Research Society |year=1963 |page=198 |isbn=}}</ref><ref name="ぬったり122p">{{Cite book|ja|author=Nuttari 300-Year Settlement Festival Executive Committee |title=Nuttari |publisher=300-Year Festival Executive Committee |year=1984 |page=122 |isbn=}}</ref>. In the Edo period, it was an object of faith for the {{ill|Mizoguchi clan|Q11564463|qid=Q11564463}} lords of {{ill|Shibata Domain|fa|قلمرو شیباتا|fr|Domaine de Shibata|ja|新発田藩|ko|시바타번|ru|Сибата (княжество)|zh|新發田藩|qid=Q1040856}}<ref name="神社辞典"/>, and Tokushō-in of the {{ill|Shingon Buddhism|Q550182|qid=Q550182}} in Nuttari served as its bettō temple<ref name="1号">{{Cite book|ja|author= |title=Kyōdo Niigata No.1 |publisher=Niigata Local History Research Society |year=1978 |page=25 |isbn=}}</ref>.

=== Precincts ===
In addition to the main sanctuary and worship hall, the precincts include subsidiary shrines, a shrine office, purification basin, dance hall, torii, a pair of komainu, and multiple stone lanterns. The oldest-dated stone lantern bears the inscription “Hakusan-gū”<ref name="現地情報"/>.

On February 5, {{ill|2016|Q25245|qid=Q25245}} (Heisei 28), a “temporary transfer festival” was held. The temporary transfer was done by the “{{ill|Structure relocation|ar|نقل المنشآت|de|Gebäudeversetzung|it|Rilocazione di strutture|ja|曳家|ko|이축|ro|Mutarea clădirilor|ru|Перемещение зданий и сооружений|ta|கட்டடம் நகர்த்தல்|tg|Ҷобаҷоии соза|uk|Перенесення споруд|zh_yue|建築物重置|qid=Q826949}}” method, moving the building without dismantling it<ref name="新潟新日報20160209"/>. This was conducted in advance of full-scale work for widening Kurinoki Bypass, to move the sacred object to a temporary shrine. It was the first time in about 170 years that the sacred object left the main sanctuary<ref name="新潟新日報20160209">{{Cite news |title=Prayers for safe movement of shrine building |newspaper=Niigata Nippo |date=2016-02-09 |author= |page=}}</ref>.

On June 12 of the same year, the building (about 11 m tall and about 50 tons) was moved about 2 m toward the approach by hikiyā work again. It was carried out with cooperation from 500 people<ref>{{Cite news |title=Residents pull ropes to shift shrine building |newspaper=Niigata Nippo |date=2016-06-14 |author= |page=}}</ref>.

The master carpenter was Kobayashi Gentarō of Kumagaya<ref name="ぬったり122p"/>. Kobayashi Gentarō was a late-Edo master artisan called Hidari Jingorō, especially known for his carvings.
* '''Principal image'''
: Eleven-faced Kannon. Year of enshrinement is unknown<ref name="第1号59p">{{Cite book|ja|author=Niigata Local History Research Society |title=Kyōdo Niigata No.1 |publisher=Niigata Local History Research Society |year=1963 |page=59 |isbn=}}</ref>.
* '''Shrine office'''
: Also called Sanshūden<ref name="現地情報"/>.
* '''Waniguchi gong'''
: Bears year inscription “Jōji 6, 丁未” (Shōhei 22, 1367 CE) and inscription of Haguro Gongen in Dewa Province<ref name="第1号59p"/>. There is a record that it was originally seized and dedicated when the Uesugi attacked Dewa in the Tenshō era, but the timing differs by one year in sources and is uncertain<ref name=第１号53p>{{Cite book|ja|author=Niigata Local History Research Society |title=Kyōdo Niigata No.1 |publisher=Niigata Local History Research Society |year=1963 |page=53 |isbn=}}</ref>.

=== Precinct shrines ===
[[File:沼垂白山神社 境内社.jpg|thumb|]]
According to its plaque, the subsidiary precinct shrine enshrines Sugawara Ōkami, Komine Ōkami, Ōyama Ōkami, Akiba Ōkami, and Awashima Ōkami together<ref name="現地情報"/>.
There are also materials listing the deities as Shinmei, Tenjin, and Inari<ref name="第1号59p"/>.

=== Outside-precinct shrine ===
[[File:沼垂白山神社 境外社.jpg|thumb|]]
Sessha:
'''Otogo Myōjin'''<ref name="第1号59p"/> (おとごみょうじん) - Deity:

=== Festivals ===
Major festivals as of 2019 are as follows<ref name="現地情報"/>.
* '''New Year Festival''' (January 1)
* '''17th Night Festival''' (January 17)<ref name="ぬったり122p"/>
: A ritual lighting large candles and praying for happiness in the coming year. Parishioners and local residents visit to pray for family safety, business prosperity, and neighborhood peace<ref>{{Cite news |title=Yearly wishes entrusted to the light |newspaper=Niigata Nippo |date=2016-01-16 |author= |page=}}</ref>.
* '''Tenjin Festival''' (February 25)
* '''Komine Festival''' (March 1)
* '''Inari Festival''' (early March)
* '''Kinen Festival''' (mid-March)
* '''Spring Festival''' (May 17–18)<ref name="ぬったり122p"/>
* '''Daisuke Festival''' (June 30)
* '''Grand Festival''' (Nuttari Festival) (August 15–18)<ref name="ぬったり122p"/>
: Has over 200 years of tradition<ref name="新潟日報2011818"/>. By day, mikoshi processions parade through the town; at night, the main event “fighting lanterns” is held<ref name="新潟日報2011818"/>. Fighting lanterns involves colliding and pushing giant lanterns; held in part of the local shopping street, and is described as full of excitement from participants supporting the lanterns and spectators shouting “Hang in there!” “Push, push!”<ref name="新潟日報2011818">{{Cite news |title=Fighting lanterns clash with heat |newspaper=Niigata Nippo |date=2011-08-18 |author= |page=}}</ref>.
* '''Shichi-go-san pilgrimage''' (November 15)
* '''Autumn Festival''' (mid-November)
* '''Daisuke Festival''' (November 31{{要検証||date=January 2024}})
* '''Monthly Festival''' (18th of every month)

=== Nuttari Festival ===
There are various theories on the origin of the Hakusan Festival, predecessor of the '''Nuttari Festival'''; its beginning dates to when the shrine was located at Ōse<ref name="まつりの起源と変遷">[https://web.archive.org/web/20181105112725/http://www.geocities.jp/nutsutarifest/yurairekisi.htm] Nuttari Festival homepage</ref>.

The schedule is basically both days corresponding to old-calendar Tanabata: August 15 (eve festival) and 16 (main festival). In the eve festival, from 19:00, over about 30 minutes, a rite transferring the divine spirit to the {{ill|Mikoshi|Q979940|qid=Q979940}} is held inside Nuttari Hakusan Shrine. In the daytime part of the main festival, the mikoshi starts from Nuttari Hakusan Shrine at 8:00 AM. In the night part, mikoshi and lanterns from each neighborhood association gather at Inari Shrine and begin from there<ref name="EVENT">[https://web.archive.org/web/20181105112734/http://www.geocities.jp/nutsutarifest/gyoujiannnai.htm] Nuttari Festival homepage
</ref>.

Since 2014, students of Higashi Niigata Junior High School have been painting lantern pictures<ref>“Love for the region put into dragons,” Niigata Nippo, Aug. 15, 2018</ref>.

The Nuttari Festival is held in the urban area of former {{ill|Nuttari|ja|沼垂町|ko|눗타리정|qid=Q11554450}}<ref group="注">Dissolved by merger in Taishō 3.</ref><ref name="MAP">[https://web.archive.org/web/20181105112734/http://www.geocities.jp/nutsutarifest/gyoujiannnai.htm] Nuttari Festival homepage
</ref>.

* {{ill|Niigata Kotsu|ja|新潟交通|qid=Q11502827}} routes '''{{ill|S9|ja|新潟交通のバス路線一覧|qid=Q11502828|lt=S9}}''' Kameda/Yokogoshi line, '''{{ill|E5|ja|新潟交通のバス路線一覧|qid=Q11502828|lt=E5}}''' Botan-yama line, '''{{ill|E6|ja|新潟交通のバス路線一覧|qid=Q11502828|lt=E6}}''' Takeo line, etc.; get off at “Nuttari Hakusan” stop<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://transfer.navitime.biz/niigatabrt-newsystem/pc/diagram/BusAboardMap?stCode=00060470|title=“Nuttari Hakusan” boarding map |publisher = Navitime|accessdate =2020-03-30}}</ref>, about 2-minute walk
